title: Saudi Coalition Downs Three Drones North of Riyadh as Sanaa Operation Looms
excerpt: Third day of attacks toward the Saudi capital; the coalition warns civilians out of a Sanaa oil site while Riyadh airport stays shut through Saturday.
body:
• The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed three drones north of Riyadh on Tuesday, spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki said.
  • The coalition also warned civilians to evacuate a Yemen Oil Company site in Sanaa ahead of a planned special operation; the Houthis threatened a harsh response in Riyadh.
  • It is the third straight day of attacks toward the Saudi capital: a Houthi ballistic missile was intercepted on Monday, and King Khalid International Airport remains shut after Saturday's deadly strike.
  • Indian airlines have cancelled Saudi flights through October 17, and the airport closure has been extended to Saturday.

Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed three drones north of Riyadh on Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition said, as the exchange of fire between the kingdom and Yemen's Houthi movement intensified for a third consecutive day.

Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki confirmed the interceptions in a statement on X, reported by IANS and Arab News. The coalition did not state who launched the drones or whether there was damage. In a separate message, Al-Maliki said the coalition would warn civilians to evacuate a site in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital Sanaa ahead of a "special operation" — identified in later statements as the Yemen Oil Company site at Al-Sabaha.

Threats traded

The Houthis responded that any attack on Sanaa would be met with harsh and painful retaliation against Riyadh. The group said on Monday evening that it had fired a ballistic missile at King Khalid International Airport, claiming a direct hit; the coalition said the missile was intercepted, and residents of the capital reported hearing explosions and receiving mobile alerts. Houthi-run Al Masirah television also reported coalition airstrikes on Saada province on Tuesday morning and said the group had shot down a Saudi drone there — claims the coalition has not confirmed.

An airport still closed

The drone interceptions come with Riyadh's airport already shut. A Houthi strike on King Khalid International Airport on Saturday killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300, according to regional reporting; a second attack on Sunday killed one person and injured 11. Saudi authorities have extended the closure until Saturday, October 17, and Indian carriers are among the airlines that have cancelled Saudi flights through that date. Ground fighting inside Yemen is also escalating, with clashes reported in Taiz province and coalition jets striking rebel positions.

Diplomatic pressure

Iran, the Houthis' main backer, said on Monday it was ready to use its good offices to facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, and Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi raised the offer with his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan on Sunday. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Iran to stop destabilising the region in a call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Tuesday, while Pakistan and Türkiye have publicly backed Riyadh.

What this means for Indian travellers and workers

Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world, and Riyadh is a major transit and work destination. With the airport closed through October 17 and airlines cancelling services, travellers with Saudi bookings this week should expect rebooking rather than travel, and check their airline's advisory before heading to any airport. There has been no announcement of an evacuation or a change to the earlier stay-indoors guidance for residents.

What's next

The coalition's promised operation in Sanaa is the immediate flashpoint: a strike on the Yemeni capital, answered as threatened, would keep Riyadh's airspace — and its Indian workforce and travellers — inside the conflict for a fourth day.
